title: Worksheet 2: Integers and Floats (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Numbers in programming are typically stored using one of two main data types: integers and floating-point numbers, often called floats. An integer is a whole number, meaning it has no fractional or decimal part, and can be positive, negative, or zero, such as 7, -42, or 0. A float, on the other hand, is a number that includes a decimal point, allowing it to represent fractional values, such as 3.14 or -0.5, which makes floats useful for situations that require more precision, like measuring distances or calculating averages. While these two types might seem similar, computers actually store and process them differently in memory, and mixing them incorrectly can sometimes cause unexpected results. For example, dividing two integers in some programming languages produces a whole number result by cutting off any remainder, called "integer division," while dividing the same two numbers as floats would produce a more precise decimal answer.
